fixes.explanation: David says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." To not want means to lack nothing he needs. I spent years in a junk drawer lacking a whole list of things, and light was at the top. David's shepherd leaves nothing off the list.

David never mentions earning anything here. He says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." The shepherd is the one who supplies what David needs. It's close to the other word, but the verse is about lacking nothing.
That one sounds close, friend. David says he lacks nothing he needs: "I shall not want." He isn't talking about keeping hold of things. He's talking about a shepherd who has him covered.

David says, "He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters." Lying down and quiet water. That's a picture of rest and peace. After my drawer years, I can tell you that sounds like a vacation.
David doesn't say the LORD tests his soul. He says, "He restores my soul…" Restoring means bringing something back to how it should be. This verse is about care.

That's it, friend. David says, "He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name." Notice whose name it is: the LORD's. David's reason for being guided points straight to the LORD Himself.
David never mentions land in this line. He says, "He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name." The reason he gives is the LORD's name. No land anywhere in the line.
David says, "You prepare a table before me…" The picture is a host setting a table for a guest. Getting ready for someone is a way of saying they matter.

Right, friend. David says, "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies." Not far from them, but in their presence. The enemies are part of the scene, and the table is still prepared for David.
